questiontext.text:
[[if test="is(cx=1)"]]On a farm in Nyandarua, the probability that a calf is vaccinated against East Coast fever is \({@pdec(p)@}\). A vaccinated calf falls ill with the disease with probability \({@pdec(q1)@}\). A calf that is not vaccinated falls ill with probability \({@pdec(q2)@}\).[[elif test="is(cx=2)"]]In Kisumu, the probability that it rains in the morning is \({@pdec(p)@}\). If it rains, Otieno arrives at school on time with probability \({@pdec(q1)@}\). If it does not rain, he arrives on time with probability \({@pdec(q2)@}\).[[elif test="is(cx=3)"]]The probability that a farmer in Trans Nzoia uses certified maize seed is \({@pdec(p)@}\). A farmer who uses certified seed harvests more than 20 bags an acre with probability \({@pdec(q1)@}\). A farmer who does not harvests more than 20 bags an acre with probability \({@pdec(q2)@}\).[[elif test="is(cx=4)"]]The probability that Chebet revises for a test is \({@pdec(p)@}\). If she revises, she passes with probability \({@pdec(q1)@}\). If she does not revise, she passes with probability \({@pdec(q2)@}\).[[/if]]

The tree diagram shows this information, with three probabilities missing.

generalfeedback.text:
(a) The branches from each point add to 1. (i) \(1 - {@pdec(p)@} = {@pdec(ta1)@}\). (ii) \(1 - {@pdec(q1)@} = {@pdec(ta2)@}\). (iii) \(1 - {@pdec(q2)@} = {@pdec(ta3)@}\).

(b) Multiply along the path [[if test="is(cx=1)"]]vaccinated[[elif test="is(cx=2)"]]rain[[elif test="is(cx=3)"]]certified seed[[elif test="is(cx=4)"]]revises[[/if]] then [[if test="is(cx=1)"]]ill[[elif test="is(cx=2)"]]on time[[elif test="is(cx=3)"]]more than 20 bags[[elif test="is(cx=4)"]]passes[[/if]]: \({@pdec(p)@} \times {@pdec(q1)@} = {@pdec(ta4)@}\).

(c) Two paths end in [[if test="is(cx=1)"]]ill[[elif test="is(cx=2)"]]on time[[elif test="is(cx=3)"]]more than 20 bags[[elif test="is(cx=4)"]]passes[[/if]]. Add them: \({@pdec(p)@} \times {@pdec(q1)@} + {@pdec(1-p)@} \times {@pdec(q2)@} = {@pdec(ta4)@} + {@pdec((1-p)*q2)@} = {@pdec(ta5)@}\).

(d) Use the complement: \(P(\)[[if test="is(cx=1)"]]not ill[[elif test="is(cx=2)"]]late[[elif test="is(cx=3)"]]20 bags or fewer[[elif test="is(cx=4)"]]fails[[/if]]\() = 1 - {@pdec(ta5)@} = {@pdec(ta6)@}\). As a check, the other two paths give \({@pdec(p*(1-q1))@} + {@pdec((1-p)*(1-q2))@} = {@pdec(ta6)@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Probability III: completing a two-stage tree diagram

Grade 12 CBE Essential 3.2: Complete the missing branches of a two-stage tree diagram whose second stage depends on the first, multiply along paths and add paths.

Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 3, Section E, question E1 of Cassell, D., Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P. and Shilton, S., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Statistics 1 for Edexcel, Cambridge University Press, 2004: a two-stage tree with a dependent second stage in four new Kenyan contexts with new numbers, randomised.
